data.exact_reserve_text:
In 2016, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 0.7m (2015: GBP 0.6m) due primarily to a reduction in claims estimates as uncertainty around catastrophe exposure unwinds. 2014 at 24 months included a reduction in respect of reserves required for Superstorm Sandy.
The movement in the net provisions for claims includes a release of GBP 0.4m (2015: GBP 0.3m).

prior_year_events.impact_description: Reduction in reserves required for Superstorm Sandy as noted at 24 months for the 2014 underwriting year

named_events.loss_description: 2014 at 24 months included a reduction in respect of reserves required for Superstorm Sandy
2014 was a benign loss year, affected only by certain Mid-West tornado activity
Significant tornado activity in Texas alongside losses from Hurricane Matthew has elevated the incurred loss ratio somewhat
Losses from Hurricane Matthew have elevated the incurred loss ratio somewhat

data.standardized_narrative: Gross prior-year reserve movement was immaterially adverse: a small gross strengthening of approximately GBP 0.014m driven by a slight upward revision to 2014 ultimates. The syndicate nonetheless reports an overall surplus in ultimate claims (GBP 0.7m) and a net release in the net provisions of GBP 0.4m, reflecting favourable development on catastrophe exposures (including a reduction in reserves related to Superstorm Sandy) after reinsurance and other adjustments.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development gross amount was derived from the gross claims development triangle (only 2014 is an older underwriting year) resulting in a very small strengthening (+GBP 0.014m). Narrative statements reference an "overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 0.7m" and a net release of GBP 0.4m (net of reinsurance), which is inconsistent with the small gross strengthening computed from the triangle. RITC commutations and translation effects may distort comparisons. Gross movement chosen from triangle per instructions; net release figures are reported elsewhere in the notes.
